Understanding the Client Context

Dr. Benson Kiarie, PhDProject Lead | CEO, Vantage Africa

About the Construction Industry Council

The Construction Industry Council (CIC) is a statutory body established under the Construction Industry Council Act No. 14 of 2013 and operating under the Ministry of Public Works and Transport. Its mandate is to regulate, develop and promote the entire construction industry value chain in Eswatini, including contractors, consultancy firms, and manufacturers and suppliers of construction materials.

In 2021, the Council adopted a three-year Construction Development Strategy (CDS) to strengthen the technical, managerial and financial capabilities of industry players, with particular emphasis on Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs). The CDS is implemented alongside the Council's Corporate Strategy, requiring coherent monitoring and reporting across both.

Strategic significance

A functional M&E system will enable the Council to demonstrate progress on the CDS to the Ministry, its Board and industry stakeholders, and to allocate resources on the basis of reliable evidence. The Council therefore requires a working system, and staff able to run it independently.

Background and Rationale for the Assignment

To assess whether the CDS is achieving its intended objectives, the Council undertook a validation of the strategy and its Implementation Plan. The exercise identified several opportunities to strengthen the M&E system that supports its implementation. First, the Council requires a structured M&E process and methodology that defines how CDS performance is tracked, by whom and how often. Second, the M&E framework must be aligned with the Corporate Strategy and other existing organisational frameworks, so that the Council monitors one coherent set of results rather than parallel systems. Third, the strategic KPIs and performance measures for the four CDS objectives need to be validated, with appropriate data sources confirmed. Fourth, monitoring of strategy implementation needs to be strengthened so that progress on priority initiatives is reviewed regularly and acted upon. Finally, and most importantly, CIC staff need the knowledge and practical skills to implement and sustain the M&E system themselves. In response, the Council seeks a firm to validate the framework, develop practical tools and build staff capacity through training, coaching and skills transfer.

How We Measure Training Effectiveness (Kirkpatrick’s Approach)

1

Reaction

What did the participants think of the training? Did they find it interesting, useful?

2

Learning

What did the participants learn from the training? We will use pre- and post-training assessments.

3

Behaviour

In what ways did the participants’ behaviour change as a result of the training? Check after 3–6 months.

4

Results

Are CIC objectives now being met better as a result of the training? Clarify specific objectives with leadership first, then evaluate.

Practical tasks are scored on one rubric: definition, data source, calculation, data quality and interpretation. Results are reported openly, including gaps.
